title: Symfony application security
description: For a Symfony application: firewalls and access control, voters, CSRF tokens, validation constraints and secrets kept out of the repository; the general rules of secure-sdlc and backend-data-safety still apply.

sources.title: Symfony 8.1, security: firewalls, access control and IsGranted
Symfony 8.1, how to use voters to check user permissions
Symfony 8.1, how to implement CSRF protection
Symfony 8.1, how to keep sensitive information secret
Symfony 8.1, configuring Symfony: environment variables and .env files

rules.instruction: Protect each route that needs a signed-in user or a role with an `access_control` rule in `config/packages/security.yaml`. List the most specific `path` first, because only the first matching rule applies, keep the firewall without a `pattern` last, and use `PUBLIC_ACCESS` only for routes that must stay open, such as the login page.
rules.verification: Write a functional test for each changed protected URL: as an anonymous visitor assert that the page is not served and the visitor is sent to log in, and as a signed-in user without the role assert a 403 response. Check that the `dev` firewall `pattern` still lists only the dev tools and asset paths.

rules.instruction: Put the permission to act on a given object, such as whether this user may edit this post, in a `Voter` with `supports()` and `voteOnAttribute()`, and check it with `#[IsGranted('edit', 'post')]` or `denyAccessUnlessGranted()`. Do not stop at a role check when the action targets one user's record.
rules.verification: Write a functional test for the changed route as a signed-in user who does not own the object and assert a 403 response, and a unit test that `supports()` returns false for other attributes and other subjects, so that the voter abstains.

rules.instruction: Keep `allow_if_all_abstain` at its default `false` under `security.access_decision_manager`, so that an attribute that no voter supports is denied instead of granted.
rules.verification: task verify evaluates the check on the working tree; review each file it names.

rules.instruction: Keep `framework.csrf_protection` enabled and give each form that changes state a CSRF token: the Form component adds and checks one by default, and a plain HTML form sends `csrf_token()` and checks it with `isCsrfTokenValid()`. Set `csrf_protection` to false only on a read-only GET form, and enable `enable_csrf` on the `form_login` of a login form.
rules.verification: Send a POST to each changed state-changing route without its token and assert that the request is rejected, and search the change for `csrf_protection` set to false: each one must be a read-only GET form.

rules.instruction: Declare validation constraints, such as `#[Assert\NotBlank]` and `#[Assert\Length]`, on each object that receives request data, and validate it through a form, the mapped request payload or `ValidatorInterface::validate()` before using or saving it. Do not hand raw request values to an entity or a query.
rules.verification: Run `php bin/console debug:validator 'App\Entity\Name'` on each changed class to list its constraints, and write a test that submits an invalid value and asserts that it is rejected and nothing is saved.

rules.instruction: Store passwords, API keys and other sensitive values in the secrets vault with `php bin/console secrets:set NAME`, or as real environment variables, and read them with `%env(NAME)%`. Keep production values out of `.env`, which holds the committed defaults for local development.
rules.verification: Run `php bin/console secrets:list` and check that each sensitive variable the change adds is listed, then search `.env` and the committed `.env.<environment>` files for production passwords, tokens and keys.

rules.instruction: List `.env.local`, `.env.*.local` and `config/secrets/prod/prod.decrypt.private.php` in `.gitignore`, and give production the decryption key through `SYMFONY_DECRYPTION_SECRET` or a file that stays on the server.
rules.verification: task verify checks that `.gitignore` names `.env.local`; run `git ls-files` and check that no `.env.local`, no `.env.*.local` file and no `prod.decrypt.private.php` is tracked.
